 entitlement process. This authority is granted under Chapter 5.32 (Street Dedication  and
 Improvement),  (Street Dedication and Improvement),  Title 5 (Streets and Sidewalks) of the
 South Gate Municipal  Code; by the California  Government  Code Section 37354 which
 authorizes a city to acquire real property for any public purpose; and by the California
 Government Code Section 66475 which authorizes a city to place exactions on private
 development such as to dedicate real property for the purpose of streets, alleys, drainage, public
 utility easements, or other public purposes. This authority was utilized to exact a dedication of
 right-of-way  from the subject development.

SUBJECT:  RESOLUTION  APPROVING  A TENATIVE  AGREEMENT  WITH  THE  SOUTH
GATE  MUNICIPAL  EMPLOYEES  ASSOCIATION  FOR  A SUCCESSOR  MOU  FOR  THE
PERIOD  JULY  1, 2021 THROUGH  JUNE  30, 2024

PURPOSE:  To  consider  a Tentative  Agreement  of  deal  points  for  a successor  labor  agreement
between  the  City  of  South  Gate  ("City")  and  the  South  Gate  Municipal  Employees  Association
[affiliated and represented by the Service Employees International Union, Local 7211 (hereinafter
collectively  "Association")  covering  the time  period  of July  1, 2021  through  June 30, 2024  ("MEA
MOU  2021-24").

RECOMMENDED  ACTION:  The  City  Council  consider  adopting  a Resolution  approving  a
Tentative  Agreement  for  a memorandum  of understanding  between  the City  of South  Gate  and the
South  Gate Municipal  Employees  Association  for the period  of July 1, 2021 through  June 30, 2024.

FISCAL  IMPACT:  The  total  cost  of the proposed  Tentative  Agreement  with  the Association  is
projected  at approximately  $2,320,000  million  for the term  of the successor  MEA  MOU,  of which
approximately  $677,000  is from  the General  Fund.  The other  costs are from  the American  Rescue
Plan Act  funds  for providing  "Essential  Worker"  compensation  for those employees  required  to work
during  the COVID-19  pandemic  time  period  (March  18, 2020,  to January  1, 2022).  A more  detailed
costing  table is provided  in Attachment  B.

ANALYSIS:  The most  recent  Memorandum  of Understanding  ("MOU")  between  the City  and the
Association  covered  the period  of July 1, 2014 through  June 30, 2015  ("SGMEA  MOU  2014-2015").
The SGMEA  MOU  2014-2015  was subsequently  extended  through  June 30, 2017,  by amendment  and
side letter.  Thereafter,  the City  and the Association  reached  a Tentative  Agreement  for  a successor
MOU  covering  the period  of July 1, 2017 through  June 30, 2020, which  was ratified  by the Association
and approved  by City  Council,  but no successor  MOU  was ever jointly  circulated  or adopted  prior  to
the expiration  of the Tentative  Agreement.  Thereafter,  the parties  informally  agreed  to maintain  the
status quo for an extra year through  June 30, 2021,  due to the ongoing  COVID-19  pandemic.

In compliance  with  the Myers-Millas-Brown  Act  ("MMBA")  codified  at Govemment  Code  Section
3500,  et seq., the labor  representatives  for the City  and the Association  commenced  negotiations  for a
new  MOU  in January  2022.  The  City  Council  was kept  apprised  of the negotiations  and provided
direction  to Staff  during  legally  noticed  Closed  Sessions.  The parties  were  able to come to a tentative

  1

  636
 agreement  on deal points  for a three-year  MOU  (July  1, 2021  through  June 30, 2024).  The Association
represents  that  it has ratified  the Tentative  Agreement  and the signatures  of the labor  representatives
thereon  reflect  a joint  recommendation  from  the negotiation  teams  of both  the City  and the Association
to the City  Council.

The  MMBA  requires  the local  legislative  body  to vote  to accept  or reject  a tentative  agreement  within
30 days of the date it is first  considered  at a duly  noticed  public  meeting.  If approved  and adopted,  the
parties  shall  then  jointly  prepare  a written  memorandum  of understanding  for  approval  by  the  City
Council  (Gov't  Code  section  3505.1).  Accordingly,  if the Tentative  Agreement  is approved  by City
Council,  then  City  Staff  and  the  Association  will  continue  to  meet  and  confer  to  create  a
comprehensive  MOU  that  is consistent  with  the prior  labor  agreements  between  the parties  and this
Tentative  Agreement  being  presented  for  approval  and  adoption,  which  MOU  will  be brought  to the
City  Council  at a future  date  for  adoption  and  approval.  The  approval  of  the  attached  Tentative
Agreement  authorizes  the  immediate  implementation  of the various  negotiated  deal  point  terms  and
conditions  of employment  of the Association  represented  employees  as specifically  provided  therein.

  Per California  Government  Code  Section  3505.1
  Between

The  most  recent  Memorandum  of  Understanding  ("MOU")  between  the  City  and  the  South  Gate
Municipal  Employees  Association  ("Association")  [affiliated  and represented  by the Service  Employees
International  Union,Local 721], was dated January 15, 2015, for the period July 1, 2014 through  June 30,
2015  ("SGMEA  MOU 2014-2015").  The SGMEA MOU 2014-2015  was subsequently  extended  through
June 30, 2017.  Thereafter,  the parties  reached  a Tentative  Agreement  for a successor  MOU covering  the
period  July 1, 2017 through  June 30, 2020,  which  was ratified  by the Association  and approved  by City
Council,  but  no  successor  MOU  was  ever  jointly  circulated  or  adopted  prior  to  the  Tentative
Agreement's  expiration.  The parties  then  informally  agreed  to maintain  the status  quo for an extra  year
through  June 30, 2021 due to the ongoing  COVID-19  pandemic.

The parties  thereafter  commenced  negotiations  on a successor  MOU, with  the first meeting  being  held
on January  27, 2022.  Just prior  to that  meeting,  the  Association  provided  its initial  proposals  for  a
successor  MOU covering  the period  July 1, 2021 through  June 30, 2024.  The parties  then met on March
23, April 19,  May 9, May 25, June 7 and June 22, 2022.  The parties  also exchanged  written  and oral
proposals  and counter  proposals,  reaching  a complete  tentative  agreement  on a successor  MOU,  the
deal points  of which  are set forth  below  and affirmed  by the execution  of this Tentative  Agreement  by
the parties'  labor representatives.  This Tentative  Agreement  was ratified  by the members  of the SGMEA
on June 28, 2022.  This Tentative  Agreement  shall not become  effective  until  accepted,  approved,  and
adopted  by the South Gate City Council  per California  Government  Code Section  3505.1,  which  provides:

  "If a tentative  agreement  is reached  by the authorized  representatives  of the public  agency  and
  a recognized  employee  organization  or recognized  employee  organizations,  the governing  body
  shall  vote  to accept  or reject  the  tentative  agreement  within  30 days  of the  date  it is first
  considered  at a duly  noticed  public  meeting.  A decision  by the  governing  body  to reject  the
  tentative  agreement  shall not bar the filing  of a charge  of unfair  practice  for failure  to meet  and
  confer  in good  faith.  If the governing  body  adopts  the tentative  agreement,  the  parties  shall
  jointly  prepare  a written  memorandum  of understanding."

  A.  RIGHT TO ADDITIONAL  COMPENSATION.
  Employees  who  are formally  appointed  to act and work  in a higher  temporarily  vacant

  1.  Minimum  Time in Classification  Requirement
  The employee  must be appointed  to work  in a temporarily  vacant  and budgeted
  higher  classification  for the requisite  time  periods  specified  below:

  appointment  start date.

  b.  If the  temporarily  vacant  and  budgeted  higher  classification  to which
  the  employee  is assigned  is vacant  due to a temporary  absence  of a
  permanent  employee,  such  as illness,  vacation,  leave  of absence,  or
  absence  without  leave, the requisite  time  period  is a cumulative  period
  of four  (4) work  weeks  in a twelve  (12) month  period  preceding  the day
  upon  which  the  employee  is appointed  to  commence  acting  in the
  higher  classification,  at which  time  the acting  pay shall be retroactive  to
  the commencement  of the appointment  start date.

 ARTICLE V, DISCIPLINE & GRIEV ANCE PROCEDURES SECTION 1 C APPEAL OF THE DISCIPLINARY ACTION
The parties  agree to retain  the services  of an Administrative  Law Judge (All)  through  the Office  of
Administrative  Hearings (OAH) to conduct  the disciplinary  action appeal and provide an advisory  written
decision in place of the City"s Personnel Officer and/or Civil Service Commission  hearings in the existing
language,  with  the City Council  having the right of review  and final decision  to accept or modify the
advisory  decision  in its sole discretion.  The City and the Association  shall share the costs of using the ALI
and OAH equally,  with each side paying their share as and when required  by the neutral,  third-party  or

the OAH.  In the event that the Association does not support an employee's appeal and/or desire to
cover half the appeal hearing costs, then the employee shall be limited to having the ALI of the OAH
issue an advisory  decision to the Personnel Officer who shall make the final decision to accept or modify
the advisory  decision  in their  sole discretion,  with the City bearing  all administrative  costs associated
with the appeal such as OAH and ALI fees, transcript fees, etc. The Association  and/or employee shall
bear their  own attorney  or other  representation  costs. If the parties  mutually  agree on an arbitrator
within thirty (30) days, that person will be designated  to conduct  the hearing instead of the ALI under
the same rules stated herein.

ARTICLE V, DISCIPLINE & GRIEV ANCE PROCEDURES SECTION 2 B GRIEV ANCE PROCEDURE
The  parties  agree  to  retain  the  services  of  an Administrative  Law Judge  through  the  Office  of
Administrative  Hearings  to conduct  the Step 4 Grievance  review  in place of the City's  Civil Service
Commission  hearing  in the existing  language,  with the City Council having the right of review  and final
decision  to accept or modify  the advisory  decision  in its sole discretion.  The City and the Association
shall share the costs of using the ALI and OAH equally,  with each side paying their share as and when
required  by the neutral,  third-party  or the OAH.  In the event that the Association  does not support  an
employee's  grievance  and/or  desire to cover half the grievance  hearing costs, then the Step 3 decision
of the Personnel  Officer  shall be final and binding  on the matter.  If the parties  mutually  agree on an
arbitrator within thirty (30) days, that person will be designated  to conduct  the hearing  instead  of the
ALI under the same rules stated herein.

FOR  THE  PERIOD  JULY  1, 2021 THROUGH  JTJNE  30, 2024

PURPOSE:  To  consider  a Tentajive  Agreement  of  deal  points  for  a successor  labor  agreement
between  the  City  of  South  Gate  ("City")  and  the  South  Gate  Professional  Mid-Management
Association  [affiliated  and represented  by  the  Service  Employees  International  Union,  Local  721]
(hereinafter  collectively  "Association")  covering  the time period  of July 1, 2021 through  June 30, 2024
("PMMA  MOU  2021-24").

RECOMMENDED  ACTION:  The  City  Council  consider  adopting  a Resolution  approving  a
Tentative  Agreement  for  a memorandum  of understanding  between  the City  of South  Gate  and the
South  Gate Professional  Mid-Management  Association  for the period  July  1, 2021  through  June 30,
2024.

FISCAL  IMPACT:  The  total  cost  of the proposed  Tentative  Agreement  with  the Association  is
projected  at  approximately  $804,000  for  the  term  of  the  successor  PMMA  MOU,  of  which
approximately  $393,000  is from  the General  Fund.  The  other  costs  are from  the American  Rescue
Plan Act  funds  for providing  "Essential  Worker"  compensation  for those  employees  required  to work
during  the COVID-19  pandemic  time  period  (March  18, 2020,  to January  1, 2022).  A more  detailed
costing  table is provided  in Attachment  B.

ANALYSIS:  The most  recent  Memorandum  of Understanding  ("MOU")  between  the City  and the
Association  covered  the  period  of July  1, 2014  through  June  30,  2015  ("SGPMMA  MOU  2014-
2015").  The  SGPMMA  MOU  2014-2015  was  subsequently  extended  through  June  30, 2017,  by
amendment  and side letter.  Thereafter,  the City  and the Association  reached  a Tentative  Agreement
for a successor  MOU  covering  the period  of July 1, 2017 through  June 30, 2020,  which  was ratified  by
the Association  and approved  by City  Council,  but no successor  MOU  was ever jointly  circulated  or
adopted  prior  to the expiration  of the Tentative  Agreement.  Thereafter,  the parties  informally  agreed to
maintain  the  status  quo  for  an extra  year  through  June  30, 2021,  due  to the  ongoing  COVID-19
pandemic.

In compliance  with  the Myers-Millas-Brown  Act  ("MMBA")  codified  at Government  Code  Section
3500,  et seq., the labor  representatives  for the City  and the Association  commenced  negotiations  for a

 new  MOU  in January  2022.  The  City  Council  was kept  apprised  of the negotiations  and provided
direction  to Staff  during  legally  noticed  Closed  Sessions.  The parties  were able to come  to a tentative
agreement  on deal points  for a three-year  MOU  (July 1, 2021 through  June 30, 2024).  The Association
represents  that it has ratified  the Tentative  Agreement  and the signatures  of the labor  representatives
thereon  reflect  a joint  recommendation  from  the negotiation  teams of both the City  and the Association
to the City  Council.

The MMBA  requires  the local  legislative  Body  to vote to accept  or reject  a tentative  agreement  within
30 days of the date it is first  considered  at a duly  noticed  public  meeting.  If approved  and adopted,  the
parties  shall  then jointly  prepare  a written  memorandum  of understanding  for  approval  by the City
Council  (Gov't  Code  section  3505.1).  Accordingly,  if the Tentative  Agreement  is approved  by City
Council,  then  City  Staff  and  the  Association  will  continue  to  meet  and  confer  to  create  a

extended  through  June 30, 2017.  Thereafter,  the  parties  reached  a Tentative  Agreement  for a successor
MOU  covering  the  period  July 1, 2017  through  June 30, 2020,  which  was ratified  by the Association  and
approved  by City  Council,  but  no successor  MOU  was  ever  jointly  circulated  or adopted  prior  to the

12,  2017,  July  24,  2018,  and  February  27, 2019.  The  parties  then  informally  agreed  to  maintain  the
status  quo for an extra  year through  June 30, 2021  due to the  ongoing  COVID-19  pandemic.

on January  27, 2022.  Just  prior  to that  meeting,  the  Association  provided  its initial  proposals  for  a
successor  MOU  covering  the  period  July 1, 2021  through  June 30, 2024.  The parties  then  met  on March
23, April  19,  May  9, May  25, June  7 and June  22, 2022.  The  parties  also exchanged  written  proposals
and counter  proposals,  reaching  a complete  tentative  agreement  on a successor  MOU,  the  deal  points
of which  are set forth  below  and affirmed  by the  execution  of this  Tentative  Agreement  by the  parties'
labor  representatives.  This Tentative  Agreement  was ratified  by the  members  of the Association  on July
13,  2022.  This Tentative  Agreement  shall  not  become  effective  until  accepted,  approved,  and adopted
by the South  Gate  City Council  per California  Government  Code  Section  3505.1,  which  provides:

  "If  a tentative  agreement  is reached  by the  authorized  representatives  of the  public  agency  and
  a recognized  employee  organization  or recognized  employee  organizations,  the governing  body
  shall  vote  to  accept  or  reject  the  tentative  agreement  within  30  days  of the  date  it is first
  considered  at a duly  noticed  public  meeting.  A decision  by the  governing  body  to  reject  the
  tentative  agreement  shall  not  bar the filing  of a charge  of unfair  practice  for failure  to meet  and
  confer  in good  faith.  If the  governing  body  adopts  the  tentative  agreement,  the  parties  shall
  jointly  prepare  a written  memorandum  of understanding."

SUBJECT:  RESOLUTION  APPROVING  A TENATIVE  AGREEMENT  WITH  THE  SOUTH
GATE  POLICE  OFFICERS'  ASSOCIATION  FOR  A SUCCESSOR  MOU  FOR  THE  PERIOD
JULY  1, 2021 THROUGH  JUNE  30, 2025

PURPOSE:  To  consider  a Tentative  Agreement  of  deal  points  for  a successor  Memorandum  of
Understanding  between  the  City  of  South  Gate  ("City")  and  the  South  Gate  Police  Officers'
Association  ("Association")  covering  the time  period  of July 1, 2021 through  June 30, 2025 ("SGPOA
MOU  2021-25").

RECOMMENDED  ACTION:  The  City  Council  consider  adopting  a Resolution  approving  a
Tentative  Agreement  for  a memorandum  of understanding  between  the City  of South  Gate  and the
South Gate Police  Officers'  Association  for the period  July 1, 2021 through  June 30, 2025.

FISCAL  IMPACT:  The  total  cost  of the proposed  Tentative  Agreement  with  the Association  is
projected  at approximately  $1,729,000  million  for  the term  of the successor  POA  MOU,  of which
approximately  $775,000  is from  the General  Fund.  The  other  costs are from  the American  Rescue
Plan Act  funds  for providing  "Essential  Worker"  compensation  for those employees  required  to work
during  the COVID-19  pandemic  time  period  (March  18, 2020,  to January  1, 2022).  A more  detailed
costing  table is provided  in Attachment  B.

ANALYSIS:  The  most  recent  Memorandum  of Understanding  ("MOU")  between  the City  and the
Association  covered  the period  of July  1, 2017  through  June  30, 2017  ("SGPOA  MOU  2017-21").
The  SGPOA  MOU  2017-21  was  subsequently  modified  by  amendment,  side letter  and/or  tentative
agreements.  In compliance  with  the Myers-Millas-Brown  Act  ("MMBA")  codified  at Government
Code Section  3500,  et seq., the parties  commenced  negotiations  on a successor  MOU  on November  4,
2021,  and thereafter  exchanged  proposals  related  thereto.  The City  Council  was kept  apprised  of the
negotiations  and provided  direction  to Staff  during  legally  noticed  Closed  Sessions.  The parties  were
able to come to a tentative  agreement  on deal points  for a four-year  MOU  (July  1, 2021 through  June
30, 2025).  The Association  represents  that it has ratified  the Tentative  Agreement  and the signatures
of the labor representatives  thereon  reflect  a joint  recommendation  from  the negotiation  teams  of both
the City  and the Association  to the City  Council.

The MMBA  requires  the local  legislative  body  to vote to accept  or reject  a tentative  agreement  within
30 days of the date it is first  considered  at a duly  noticed  public  meeting.  If approved  and adopted,  the

 parties  shall  then jointly  prepare  a written  memorandum  of understanding  for  approval  by the City
Council  (Gov't  Code  section  3505.1).  Accordingly,  if the Tentative  Agreement  is approved  by City
Council,  then  City  Staff  and  the  Association  will  continue  to  meet  and  confer  to  create  a
comprehensive  MOU  that  is consistent  with  the prior  labor  agreements  between  the parties  and this
Tentative  Agreement  being  presented  for  approval  and adoption,  which  MOU  will  be brought  to the
City  Council  at a future  date  for  adoption  and  approval.  The  approval  of the  attached  Tentative
Agreement  authorizes  the immediate  implementation  of the various  negotiated  deal point  terms  and
conditions  of employment  of the Association  represented  employees  as specifically  provided  therein.

SUBJECT:  RESOLUTION  APPROVING  A TENATIVE  AGREEMENT  WITH  THE SOUTH

2021 THROUGH  JUNE 30, 2025

PURPOSE:  To consider a Tentative Agreement of deal points for a successor labor agreement
between the City of South Gate ("City")  and the South Gate Police Management Association
("Association")  covering the time period of July 1, 2021 through June 30, 2025 ("SGPMA  MOU
2021-25").

RECOMMENDED  ACTION:  The City Council consider adopting a Resolution  approving a
Tentative Agreement for a memorandum of understanding between the City of South Gate and the
South Gate Police Management Association for the period July 1, 2021 through June 30, 2025.

FISCAL  IMPACT:  The total cost of the proposed Tentative Agreement with the Association  is
projected at approximately $777,000 for the term of the successor PMA MOU, of which approximately
$502,000 is from the General Fund. The other costs are from the American Rescue Plan Act funds for
providing "Essential Worker" compensation for those employees required to work during the COVID-
19 pandemic time period (March 18, 2020, to January 1, 2022).  A more detail costing table is
provided  in Attachment B.

ANALYSIS:  The most recent Memorandum of Understanding ("MOU")  between the City and the
Association covered the period of July 1, 2005 through June 30, 2008 ("SGPMA MOU 2005-2008").
The SGPMA MOU 2005-2008 was subsequently extended through June 30, 2017, by amendment
and/or side letter.  Thereafter, the City and the Association reached a Tentative Agreement for a
successor comprehensive MOU covering the period of July 1, 2017 through June 30, 2020, which was
ratified by the Association and approved by City Council, but no successor MOU was ever jointly
circulated or adopted prior to the expiration of the Tentative Agreement.  Therea'fter, the parties
informally  agreed to maintain the status quo for an extra year through June 30, 2021, due to the
ongoing  COVID-19 pandemic.

In compliance with the Myers-Millas-Brown  Act ("MMBA")  codified at Government Code Section
3500, et seq., the labor representatives for the City and the Association commenced negotiations for a
new MOU in March 2022. The City Council was kept apprised of the negotiations and provided
direction to Staff during legally noticed Closed Sessions. The parties were able to come to a tentative

 agreement  on deal points for a four-year MOU (July 1, 2021 through June 30, 2025).
  The Association
represents  that it has ratified the Tentative Agreement and the signatures of the labor representatives
thereon reflect  a joint recommendation  from the negotiation teams of both the City and the Association
to the City Council.

The MMBA requires the local legislative body to vote to accept or reject a tentative
  agreement within
30 days of the date it is first considered at a duly noticed public meeting. If approved
  and adopted, the
parties shall then jointly prepare a written memorandum of understanding for
  approval by the City

Council,  then City Staff and the Association  will continue to meet and confer to create a
comprehensive  MOU that is consistent with the prior labor agreements between the parties and
  this
Tentative  Agreement being presented for approval and adoption, which MOU will be brought
  to the
City  Council  at a 'future date for adoption and approval. The approval of the attached Tentative
Agreement  authorizes  the irnrnediate implementation  of the various negotiated deal point terms and
conditions  of employment of the Association represented employees as specifically provided

  Between

The most  recent  Memorandum  of Understanding  ("MOU")  between  the City and the South  Gate Police
 Management  Association  ("Association")  expired  on June 30, 2008  ("SGPOA  MOU  2005-08")(Contract
 No. 2265).  Thereafter,  the  parties  entered  into  various  Amendments  and Side Letters  covering  the
 period  July 1, 2008  through  June 30, 2017.  On December  12,  2017,  the City and Association  entered
into  an Amended  and Restated  Tentative  Agreement  for a Successor  Memorandum  of Understanding
 ("ARTA")  which  provided  that  all terms  and conditions  of the SGPMA  MOU  2005-2008,  including  any
amendments  thereto,  and Side Letter  Agreements,  shall  be maintained  unless  expressly  modified  or
changed  by the ARTA or until  the successor  2017-20  MOU was approved  accepted  and adopted  by the
City Council.  The  successor  2017-2020  MOU  was never  prepared,  and additional  Side Letters  were
entered  into between  the parties.  The parties  informally  agreed  to maintain  the status  quo through  the
initial  COVID 19 pandemic  through  June 30, 2022.

On March  23, 2022,  the Association  made  a formal  request  to commence  negotiations  on a successor
labor  agreement  prior  to June 30, 2022.  The parties  commenced  negotiations  on May 26, 2022,  with
the  Association  providing  its initial  proposal  for  a successor  MOU.  Thereafter,  the  parties  met  and
exchanged  proposals  related  thereto.  The parties  reached  a Tentative  Agreement  for a successor  MOU
the deal points  of which  are set forth  below  and affirmed  by the execution  of this Tentative  Agreement
by the  parties'  labor  representatives.  This Tentative  Agreement  was ratified  by the  members  of the
Association  on July 14,  2022.  This Tentative  Agreement  shall  not  become  effective  until  accepted,
approved,  and adopted  by the South  Gate City Council  per California  Government  Code Section  3505.1,
which  provides:

  "If a tentative  agreement  is reached  by the authorized  representatives  of the public  agency  and
  a recognized  employee  organization  or recognized  employee  organizations,  the governing  body
  shall  vote  to accept  or reject  the  tentative  agreement  within  30 days  of the  date  it is first
  considered  at a duly  noticed  public  meeting.  A decision  by the  governing  body  to reject  the
  tentative  agreement  shall not bar the filing  of a charge  of unfair  practice  for failure  to meet  and
  confer  in good  faith.  If the  governing  body  adopts  the tentative  agreement,  the  parties  shall
  jointly  prepare  a written  memorandum  of understanding."

Any items  within  the SGPMA  MOU 2005-08,  the subsequent  Amendments  or Tentative  Agreements  or
Side  Letters  or any  other  current  labor  agreements  not  addressed  herein  are  proposed  to  remain
unchanged  until  such time  as the successor  PMA MOU is ratified  by the Association  and approved  and
adopted  by City Council;  however,  any contractual  language  that  has a specific  end date will be deemed
of no further  force  and effect.  The parties  have agreed  that  the consolidated  successor  MOU shall be
prepared  and submitted  to City Council  for adoption  as soon as practicable,  but in no event  later than
sixty (60) days from  City Council  approval  of this Tentative  Agreement.

 PREAMBLE
 The  following  language  shall  be in the  successor  MOU  and  replace  any  similar  language  from  prior
 agreements:

  This  Agreement  is a good  faith  effort  by the  Association  and  City  to  consolidate  decades  of
  individual  MOUs  and side agreements  into  this one  comprehensive  document.  It is possible  that
  provisions  of  the  MOUs and/or  side agreements  or related  resolutions  may  have  been
  inadvertently  omitted  in the  comprehensive  MOU.  Therefore,  each  party  to this  MOU  reserves
  its rights  to  bring  to the  other  party's  attention  a provision  in a prior  MOU  or still  valid  side
  agreement  or resolution  that  is not  included  in this  MOU.  In such  case,  the  parties  agree  to
  convene  meetings  to  address  the  issue  and  to  engage  in  good  faith  attempts  to  reach
  agreement  as to  the validity  and/or  content  of  any such  omitted  evidence  of terms  and
  conditions  of employment.  No representation  is made  that  such  agreement(s)  shall  be arrived
  at.

  Additionally,  in preparing  this  MOU,  it is not  the  intent  of the  parties  to invalidate  terms  and
  conditions  of employment  that  are not set forth  in this  MOU,  but which  are referenced  in a still
  valid  side agreement  or past practice  as this term  is defined  by statutory  and case law.

TERM
The  following  language  shall  be in the  successor  MOU  and  replace  any  similar  language  from  prior
agreements:

  This  Agreement  shall  be effective  from  July 1, 2021  through  June  30, 2025  (4 years)  and  shall
  supersede  the  SGPMA  MOU  2005-08  and  any  Side  Letters  entered  into  during  or after  the
  adoption  of the SGPMA  MOU  2005-08,  which  are intended  to be incorporated  in this Agreement
  if to be continued.  The  MOU  shall  become  effective  only  after  adoption  by the  City Council  of
  the  City of South  Gate  following  ratification  by the  members  of the  Association.  The terms  of
  this  Agreement  shall  only  apply  to those  employees  still on payroll  at the time  that  it is adopted
  by City Council,  with  the exception  of retiree  benefits.

 SICK LEAVE
The following  further  changes  are implemented  and shall  be made  to the  successor  MOU  provision  and
replace  any previous  similar  or related  provisions:

  SICK LEAVE CONVERSION

  The  City  shall  permit  represented  PMA  employees  who  are  in the  final  3 years  of an eligible
  employee"s  employment  before  attaining  the  Normal  Retirement  Age  as  defined  by  IRS
  regulations  and have  20 or more  years  with  the  City to convert  accrued  unused  sick leave  prior
  to  retirement  for  the  purpose  of  maximizing  the  employee"s  "Catch  Up"  contributions  to
  Deferred  Compensation,  as permitted  by applicable  provisions  of the  Internal  Revenue  Code.

  The Conversion  of accrued  unused  sick leave  hereunder  shall  be at the employee's  Regular  Rate
  of Pay as defined  in this  MOU.  This sick leave  conversion  to deferred  compensation  is limited  to
  a maximum  of 1200  hundred  hours  for  both  conversion  to deferred  compensation  and for cash
  out  upon  separation.  Any  remaining  sick leave  hours  balance  above  the  combined  1200  hour
  cap  can  still  be converted  to  retirement  credit  to the  extent  the  City  maintains  that  CalPERS
  contract  benefit.  Effective  with  the pay period  commencing  July 30, 2022,  new  hires  shall  not be
  entitled  to convert  sick leave  to deferred  compensation  or cash out.  Recruits  in the Academy  are
  not  deemed  employees  for  this  purpose.  Any  represented  employee  that  dies  prior  to
  retirement  shall  have  their  sick leave  paid  to their  beneficiary  if the  employee  has 20 or more
  years  of service  at the time  of death  or if the death  was work  related.

  SICK LEAVE CASH OUT UPON  SEPARATION

  PMA  represented  employees  hired  prior  to  July 1, 1993  shall  be permitted  to  cash  out  an
  unlimited  number  of accrued  unused  sick leave  hours.

  PMA  represented  employees  hired  on  or after  July 1, 1993  shall  be permitted  to  cash  out  a
  lifetime  maximum  of twelve  hundred  (1200)  accrued  unused  sick  leave  hours.  Cash  out  of
  accrued  unused  sick leave  hours  shall  be at the employee's  Regular  Rate of Pay as defined  in this
  MOU.

  This  sick  leave  cash  out  upon  separation  is limited  to a maximum  of 1200  hundred  hours  for
  both  cash out  upon  separation  and conversion  to deferred  compensation.  Any  remaining  sick
  leave  hours  balance  above  the  combined  1200  hour  cap can  still  be converted  to  retirement
  credit  to the  extent  the  City  maintains  that  CalPERS  contract  benefit.  Effective  with  the  pay
  period  commencing  July  30,  2022,  new  hires  shall  not  be entitled  to  convert  sick  leave  to
  deferred  compensation  or cash out.  Recruits  in the Academy  are not deemed  employees  for this
  purpose.

SUBJECT:  RENAMING  THE  SOUTH  GATE  PARK  MUNICIPAL  AUDITORIUM  AFTER
FORMER  MAYOR  HENRY  C. GONZALEZ

PURPOSE:  This  item  was requested  to be placed  on the agenda  by Mayor  AI  Rios  and Council
Member  Maria  Davila  to discuss  whether  direction  should  be given  to rename  the South  Gate Park
Municipal  Auditorium  in  memory  of  former  Mayor  Heru'y  C.  Gonzalez  in  recognition  of  his
contributions  to the community  and service  on the City  Council.

RECOMMENDED  ACTION:  The City  Council  will  consider:
  A. Giving  staff  direction  to  bring  back  a formal  resolution  to  the  City  Council  to  consider
  dedicating  and naming  the South  Gate Park Municipal  Auditorium  as the Henry  C. Gonzalez
  Municipal  Auditorium;  and
  B.  Placing  a plague  stating  the role former  Mayor  Henry  C. Gonzalez  played  and contributions  he
  made to the City  of South  Gate during  his nearly  three decades of service.

FISCAL  IMPACT:  The total  costs for purchasing  a bronze  plague  and changing  the name  on the
auditorium  building  is estimated  at $15,000.

ANALYSIS:  Former  Mayor  Heruy  C. Gonzalez  was first  elected  to the South  Gate City  Council  in
April  1982,  which  started  his historic  27-year  careers  as an elected  official.  In 1983,  he made history
by becoming  the  first  Latino  to serve  as Mayor  of the  City  of  South  Gate,  a position  he would
ultimately  hold a total  of seven times  during  his career on the South Gate City  Council.

Mayor  Gonzalez  also dedicated  his life  to supporting  the youth  in the community.  He founded  the
South  Gate High  School  Booster  Club  and the South  Gate-Youth  Football  program.  He also served  as
the District  Chairman  for the Boy  Scouts  of America.

Mayor  Gonzalez  touched  numerous  lives  and was known  as a beacon  of light,  setting  the highest
standards  for political  ethics  and integrity  in the region  and fought  to keep  South  Gate free of cornipt
influence  during  his entire  career.

This  request  has also received  support  from  many  of the residents  of South  Gate as well  as leaders
from  Congress,  the State Assembly,  and the County  Board  of Supervisors.

minutes_text:
CITY OF SOUTH GATE
  REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  MINUTES
  TUESDAY, JULY 26, 2022
CALL TO ORDER  Al Rios, Mayor called a Regular City Council Meeting to order at 6:34
  p.m.

INVOCATION  Steve Costley, Interim Director of Parks & Recreation
PLEDGE OF
ALLEGIANCE  Roxaynn Robinson, Revenue Manager

ROLL CALL  Yodit Glaze, City Clerk

PRESENT  Mayor Al Rios, Vice Mayor Maria del Pilar Avalos, Council Member
  Denise Diaz, and Council Member Gil Hurtado; Interim City Manager
  Chris Jeffers, City Attorney Counsel Raul F. Salinas

EXCUSED  Council Member Maria Davila
LATE  City Treasurer Gregory Martinez arrived at 6:35 p.m.
1
PERSONNEL RECRUITMENT
& SELECTION  The City Council considered the list of new and promotional full-time
  employees hired or promoted during June 2022.

2
PROPERTY USE
ADMIN/PERMITS  The City Council conducted a public hearing and approved item 2(A) by
  motion of Council Member Hurtado and seconded by Vice Mayor Avalos.

  ROLL CALL: Council Member Diaz, yes; Council Member Hurtado,
  yes; Vice Mayor Avalos, yes; Mayor Rios, yes; Council Member Davila,
  yes.

  a.  Adopting Resolution No. 2022-40-CC entitled Resolution of the City
  Council of the City of South Gate, California, upholding the
  Planning Commission's decision to deny Conditional Use Permit No.
  860 for an Alcoholic Beverage Control license (Type 41 On-Sale
  Beer and Wine-Eating Place) to sell beer and wine at the Goals
  Soccer Facility and approve revised conditions of approval for hours
  of operation and compliance review requirements; or

  b.  Adopting Resolution overturning the Planning Commission's
  decision to deny Conditional Use Permit No. 860 for an Alcoholic
  Beverage Control license (Type 41 On Sale Beer and Wine - Eating
  Place) to sell beer and wine at the Goals Soccer Facility and approve
  revised conditions of approval for hours of operation and compliance
  review requirement.
   REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES OF JULY 26, 2022

3
MUNICIPAL CODE
ADMIN  The City Council conducted a Public Hearing and approved items A & B
  by motion of Council Member Hurtado and seconded by Council Member
  Diaz.

  ROLL CALL: Council Member Diaz, yes; Council Member Hurtado,
  yes; Vice Mayor Avalos, yes; Mayor Rios, yes; Council Member Davila,
  excused.

  a.  Waiving the reading in full and introducing Ordinance No. 2022-
  07-CC entitled Ordinance of the City Council of the City of South
  Gate, California, amending Chapter 11.33 (Parking Standards), of
  Title 11 (Zoning), of the SGMC to include parking requirements
  and standards for land uses serving children, older adults,
  community assembly or people with disabilities; and

  b.  Accepting the determination that the proposed amendment is
  Exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA)
  pursuant to the Public Resources Code Section 21080.17.

DEVIATE FROM
THE AGENDA  At this time, there being no objections, Mayor Rios stated that item 19
  would be considered out of its regular agenda order.
19
AUDITORIUM ADMIN  The City Council considered:

  a.  Giving staff direction to bring back a formal resolution to the City
  Council to consider dedicating and naming the South Gate Park
  Municipal Auditorium as the Henry C. Gonzalez Municipal
  Auditorium; and

  b.  Placing a plaque stating the role former Mayor Henry C. Gonzalez
  played and contributions he made to the City of South Gate during
  his nearly three decades of service.

  Council Member Davila requested that this item be continued to the next
  meeting so she would be able to participate in the discussion and vote.

  This item was continued to the City Council Meeting of August 9th.

RECESS  City Council took a 5-minute break.

  Page 2 of 14
   REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES OF JULY 26, 2022
COMMENTS FROM
THE AUDIENCE  Jesus Miranda spoke about the reduction of time in speaking. He expresses
  that they are trying to take the right of the people to speak up and would
  like to know why. Asks council to please consider keeping it at five
  minutes instead of reducing it. Also states that Councilwoman Davila is
  not here, and she should be here and recalls the history of corruption in the
  city and does not plan to leave the city.

  Marco Torres with Neu-Self Awakening it is a new non-profit
  organization focusing on mental health and behavioral health. Explains
  that communities are faced with mental health crisis and explain some of
  the reasons such as access and cultural awareness. He explains what the
  non-profit is and the way they help the people that come into there office.
  They are looking to make South Gate one of there corporate office
  location for the much-needed mental health resources in the area. The
  health resources and service administration has recognized the south cities
  specifically South Gate as an area shortage of mental health provider.
  They are looking to partner with the local universities to bring in recent
  graduates that will be monitored by licensed therapists, not only to
  complete there hours but to serve the communities that they come from.
  He talks about his personal experience when it comes to dealing with
  mental health issues and he is also a resident of south-central LA, and he
  has 32 years of experience in health care. He came so that everyone could
  get to know him and the program and invites them to sit with him and
  learn about their mental and behavioral model.

  Carlos Amador thanks the chief for taking the time to talk to him
  regarding some of the issues he had. He appreciates when city employees
  take the time to listen. He is here because in his street there hasn't been
  street cleaning for about a year, he has been the one cleaning the streets
  and the gutters. He contacted the city and the city manager, he said he
  would investigate it, but nothing happens, and he is still billed for street
  cleaning. Expresses his frustration because he is paying for a service that
  he does not get and that he does himself.

  Thomas Buckley says he is incredibly disappointed that they limited the
  speech to three minutes, and he doesn't think there is any considerable
  time saving. Explains that communication is important in any relationship
  and limiting the speech diminishes the relationship between the residents
  and council and asks that in the future they reconsider this. Says that last
  council meeting there was a lengthy discussion about the parks division,
  and he was hoping to talk about it today. Thursday, he emailed to see if it
  was going to be on the agenda to talk about today and City Manager
  Jeffers replied and stated that he and the City Attorney were unsuccessful
  in procuring the information needed in a timely manner and it will be
  addressed in the next meeting. The City Manager explains that technically
  the city council doesn't need to have a resolution on this matter up until
  the city formally accepts the results. Addresses the city clerk position and

  Page 3 of 14
   REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES OF JULY 26, 2022

COMMENTS FROM
THE AUDIENCE CONT'D  the idea of having a deputy city clerk and he believes that all the good
  candidates have moved on. He really hopes that the council considered the
  residents and respect the way they vote.

  Mario Dominguez asks who is the person that picks the agenda items
  because the meeting have been getting longer and longer. He says that the
  council needs to look at how they are running these meetings. He believes
  that they are doing to much and thinks that they could get more done if
  they had less things to get through. He suggests the City Manager should
  be giving the Council Members updates weekly so they know what they
  have in the books.

  Adolfo Varas finds the idea of getting a deputy city clerk alarming
  because he thinks it is a waste of taxpayer dollars. He explains that they
  already have a city clerk. He also finds alarming the reduction in time that
  residents can speak, says that council is there to serve the community
  regardless of the hours. He is hoping that the council will reconsider
  changing the time in the future and consider some of the things they are
  doing.

  Jovanna Laborin thanked Steven and his staff for all he does. She shares
  her concerns about the things that have been going on at the park, they
  have been reporting illegal fireworks and they have about four counts of
  fires that they have started, vandalism, and children that smoke at the park
  which spreads in the park. She is concerned for the safety of the
  community and hopes that Steve and the chief can help them out at the
  park. She also had a visit from the health department at the snack bar
  because somebody got sick from something that was purchased behind a
  van. She explains that now there are vehicles that park around the park and
  open the back of their cars and start selling. They also have two cart
  vendors that sell items, but they are sealed.

  Liz Ruiz gave an update on the meetings that she attended this month. As
